---
title: "Week 2 Case Studies: Communication in Organizations"
---

Each group will work through one organization in depth, then present their analysis to the class. You have about 20 minutes to work through the questions; plan on a 3–4 minute presentation.

## The Organizations

- **Group A:** [KAPOW — a manufacturing plant](case-study-week-02-factory.html)
- **Group B:** [Midland Metro Transit — a city bus system](case-study-week-02-transit.html)
- **Group C:** [Homes for All Coalition — a housing justice organization](case-study-week-02-social-movement.html)

---

## Questions (same for all groups)

Work through these in order. Be specific — use details from your organization's scenario.

**1. Identify communication**

What are *all* the kinds of communication that have to occur for your organization to function? Think broadly: who talks to whom, through what channels, about what? Try to list at least 8–10 distinct types.

**2. What does communication *do* here?**

Pick 2–3 items from your list and analyze what communication is actually accomplishing — not just passing information, but coordinating action, establishing authority, building identity, motivating people, resolving conflict, etc. Use concepts from Ch. 1.

**3. Forces of change**

How has your organization changed — or how *will* it change — because of each of the following? Be as specific as you can:

- **Globalization** — supply chains, competition, migration, offshoring, global customers
- **Climate change** — operations, mission, risk, regulation, stakeholder pressure
- **Changing demographics** — workforce, customer base, leadership, community
- **Changing technology** — how work gets done, how people communicate, what jobs exist

---

## Presentations

Make a ~5 minute presentation about your organization and your analysis. Be sure to include:
- A brief description of the organization and its context
- An explanation of the communication you identified and what it accomplishes
- A discussion of how the organization has changed or will change because of the forces above
